newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Aug/Sep gas oil done at -30cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Aug/Sep gas oil done at -30cts.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up late afternoon on Friday ending a week where it had gained more than $1.50 per barrel on a firm note after unexpected buying emerged, traders said.

The strong front month buying interest as also lead to a sharp narrowing of the August/September spread to trade at minus 30 cents but traders said the market is unlikely to revert into backwardation within the new few days.
August swaps were last quoted at $23.20/$23.30 per barrel, up slightly from Thursday's $23.10/$22.20, brokers said.
August traded earlier in the day at $23.20. It traded at an intra-week high of $23.50 late Thursday compared to a traded low of $21.50 on Friday.
September swaps on the other hand edged down slightly to last quoted at $23.45/$23.55 from Thursday's $23.55/$22.65. It traded earlier in the day at $23.50.

As a result the August/September time spread narrowed and traded earlier in the day at minus 30 cents compared to an early week trade of minus 70 cents and deals on Thursday at minus 44 cents, brokers said.
Traders said the market is unlikely to flip into backwardation due to the large prompt physical supplies in Singapore and poor demand from China.
Singapore middle distillate stocks for the week ending July 23 rose by 469,000 barrels to 11.084 million, the Trade Development Board said on Thursday.
But despite this an unexpected prompt buying binge contributed to the soaring swaps prices which was also helped along the way by East-West paper players.
Traders said about 1.1 million barrels of physical gas oil traded so far this week by players looking to cover short sales especially to Indonesia.

The latest trade was on Thursday when a Dutch trader bought a 150,000-barrel cargo from a European major at $22.75 per barrel, up 85 cents from Wednesday's traded high of $21.90 and $1.45 more than the day-earlier traded low of $21.30.
The strong gas oil combined with a moderately firm jet fuel has lead to a sharp narrowing of the jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade.
The August regrade was last quoted at $1.25/$1.40 per barrel from Thursday's $1.40/$1.50, brokers said. August traded on late Thursday at $1.45 and $1.35 per barrel, they said.
The prices are well off the $1.80/$2.00 quoted on Monday.
August fuel oil midday Friday was quoted at $99.50/$100.00 per tonne, up 50 cents from Thursday after values rose on firm bids late Thursday.
